questions.q: Why is inactivating generally preferred over deleting a supplier, site, or bank account that's no longer used?
options: Deleting is always faster
Inactivating preserves transaction history and the audit trail while preventing new activity
Inactivating automatically merges the record with another supplier
There is no real difference between the two
questions.explain: Inactivating stops new transactions while keeping past invoices and payments intact and reportable.

questions.q: Which of these is a common real-world cause of duplicate supplier records?
options: A supplier's business classification expiring
A supplier site being inactivated
An invoice being matched three-way instead of two-way
The same real company being entered twice under slightly different names
questions.explain: Duplicates often arise from re-entering the same company under a different name, or from one company acquiring another.

questions.q: What does a supplier merge actually do?
options: It consolidates one supplier or site into another, moving transaction references to the surviving record
It deletes both supplier records entirely
It automatically changes the surviving supplier's tax registration
It converts the supplier from Prospective to Spend Authorized
questions.explain: A merge moves purchase order and invoice references from the old record onto the surviving one.

questions.q: Why might Payables refuse to transfer a specific invoice during a supplier merge?
options: The invoice is not yet due
The invoice has a business classification attached
Transferring it would create a duplicate invoice (same number, same supplier) on the surviving record
The invoice was paid by check instead of EFT
questions.explain: Fusion protects against creating duplicate invoices on the surviving supplier, so a conflicting invoice number will not transfer.

questions.q: What is the key practical reason to carefully review both supplier records before submitting a merge request?
options: A merge is treated as irreversible once completed
Merges are automatically reviewed by Oracle support
Merging always deletes all open invoices
Review is only needed for international suppliers
questions.explain: Because a merge can't be undone, reviewing open invoices, balances, and site assignments beforehand avoids leaving items stranded on the retired record.
